transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-28 14:05 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Lara Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sanjay Patel (Argonaut CTO), Marta Gómez (Platform Eng), Ethan Ross (SRE)

Summary: quick discovery on p95 targets and peak throughput for streaming conversational product. Customer is evaluating Hosted first but wants deterministic p95 at scale; interested in Dedicated and Private for data residency/KMS. Ask for benchmark runs and security docs, plan pilot.

--- Transcript body ---
00:00 Lara Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we've got about an hour, quick intros?
00:07 Sanjay Patel: sanjay here, CTO at argonaut, we run the PeakFlow inference stack, responsible for production latency goals.
00:12 Marta Gómez: marta, platform eng, i'll be owning the POC work.
00:15 Ethan Ross: ethan, SRE, i'll be verifying the p95 numbers and infra constraints.
00:19 Lara Chen: perfect. mateo, wanna intro yourself?
00:21 Mateo Ruiz: yeah hi, mateo, solution engineer, i focus on latency tooling and benchmark harnesses at redwood.
00:26 Lara Chen: goal today is to map your p95 targets, concurrency, and streaming patterns so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private and propose an experiment.
00:34 Sanjay Patel: brief context — we have a conversational assistant embedded in our customer dashboard. typical session is 6–8 turns, average prompt length around 1.2k tokens, but we have long reports that hit up to 8k tokens for summarization flows. Peak QPS currently about 120 sustained but occasional bursts to 1.5k qps for 30–90s during report generation windows. p95 target we're aiming for is sub-450ms for short-turn chat, and under 1.2s for the longer summarization streaming output.
01:05 Lara Chen: okay, that's helpful. couple clarifying q's: are you planning synchronous streaming to browser clients?
01:10 Marta Gómez: yes, streaming via websockets, client expects progressive tokens. we consider partial results acceptable. cold-starts are a problem — p95 spikes when cache is empty.
01:18 Mateo Ruiz: got it. how much of that traffic must be within data residency/air-gapped constraints? any KMS requirements?
01:24 Sanjay Patel: all production data for EU customers must stay in our VPC in eu-west-1. we use cloud-kms (customer-managed) and require audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. SOC2 necessary, and SSO via SAML is a must.
01:35 Lara Chen: that's common — we support VPC private and on-prem options and integrate with customer KMS and audit log sinks. i'll share the security pack.
01:41 Ethan Ross: quick intimidating part — we run mixed workloads, interactive chat with short seq and a smaller percent of long summarization flows. We need to size for concurrency: typical sustained concurrency ~450 simultaneous sessions, but bursts cause 3k concurrent token streams briefly. can you explain how redwood batches and handles KV cache for streaming?
02:00 Mateo Ruiz: sure — our runtime uses continuous batching and per-model KV cache; for streaming we do prefix caching where applicable and maintain hot-shard routing for low-latency sessions. in practice, batching reduces per-token cost but can increase latency if you set batching windows too big — we tune batch targets to meet p95. for your short-turn p95 target of 450ms we'd recommend conservative batch windows and smaller batch sizes or prioritization tiers for interactive traffic.
02:26 Sanjay Patel: is there automatic fallback if dedicated capacity is exhausted? what happens during a 1.5k qps burst?
02:33 Lara Chen: yes — policies can tier traffic. Hosted customers can opt for overflow to wider multi-tenant pools, or Dedicated setups can have burst capacity or cross-region failover. worst case we fallback to a compatible quantized model variant with higher latency but still functional. we can show latency delta numbers in the benchmark.
02:49 Marta Gómez: the delta numbers are critical. can you run token/sec benchmarks with our real model artifacts? we want realistic p95 numbers with streaming token pacing.
02:56 Mateo Ruiz: absolutely — we asked you to provide a representative prompt set and model binary. we can run 3 runs: steady-state, burst ramp, and cold-start stress. each run will capture per-token latency traces, p95, p99, and per-shard utilization.
03:09 Sanjay Patel: timeline? we ideally want results next week to feed our infra decision in mid-March.
03:15 Lara Chen: we can prioritize that. mateo can you commit to a 3–5 day turnaround once we have artifacts and credentials?
03:21 Mateo Ruiz: yes assuming we get a small VM/docker image or model weights and a 1–2GB sample of prompts. we'll need a simple harness script or we can adapt your prompts into ours. 3–5 business days likely.
03:33 Ethan Ross: what about streaming tokens/sec versus generation rate? our client paces display faster than model emits sometimes — any suggestions?
03:39 Mateo Ruiz: you can do token prefetching with partial decode, but the runtime must keep kv cache pinned. we also recommend a small client buffer and backpressure signals. on the server side we expose a streaming SLO meter and per-token emit latency metrics so you can correlate display lag vs model emit.
03:55 Sanjay Patel: curious about cost tradeoffs — Dedicated looks attractive for predictability, but we also want to keep unit cost reasonable. how do you recommend sizing?
04:03 Lara Chen: sizing aligns to sustained qps + desired headroom and burst handling. Dedicated is best when you have predictable sustained throughput; Hosted is better for variable workloads with smaller steady-state. For your profile — sizable sustained concurrency (~450) plus dramatic burst — a hybrid is common: Dedicated for baseline traffic with Hosted overflow for bursts. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching settings per workload to lower unit cost.
04:28 Marta Gómez: given our security needs (VPC + CMK), would Dedicated in our VPC be possible? or do we need Private?
04:34 Lara Chen: we offer Redwood Dedicated with customer VPC peering and options for customer-managed keys. For strict air-gapped requirements, the Private on-prem package is the route. From what you describe (VPC + CMK + SIEM), Dedicated with VPC wiring typically suffices.
04:49 Ethan Ross: any examples of p95 numbers for 8k sequence summarization on a 24GB GPU?
04:55 Mateo Ruiz: approximate numbers — for a 24GB A10-style GPU with optimized kernels and int8 quantization, end-to-end token emit p95 for long 8k seq streaming depends heavily on context reuse. Cold path full 8k summarization might be in 1.1–1.6s p95 per chunk, while incremental streaming token-by-token could meet your 1.2s service-level for progressive output if we do prefix caching and model slicing. i'll caveat: those are broad approximations — we'll run the exact benchmark on your model.
05:28 Sanjay Patel: how do you handle model variants and fallbacks? we can't have a too-low-quality model in failover.
05:35 Lara Chen: we recommend a graded family of variants vetted via evals. Fallback policies are rule-driven: if latency > threshold, route to a smaller variant that maintains acceptable quality. Redwood's rollouts can do canary testing to ensure fallbacks don't regress user experience.
05:48 Marta Gómez: operationally, what telemetry do we get during POC?
05:52 Mateo Ruiz: access to the Console for the pilot: per-route token-level latencies, p95/p99, per-shard GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates, and streaming emit histograms. we'll also share raw trace files and a benchmarking spreadsheet with parsed percentiles.
06:08 Ethan Ross: on networking — we use private connectivity with NAT restrictions. can redwood run benchmarks inside our VPC or do we tunnel traffic?
06:16 Lara Chen: we can run the POC in your VPC via a Private pilot, or we can run tests from our infra with a mirrored environment. for an accurate p95 and networking latency test, running inside your VPC gives the most fidelity.
06:27 Sanjay Patel: cool. about acceptance criteria — we'll consider the POC successful if 95% of short-turn sessions meet <450ms p95 and long-form summarization stays under 1.2s p95 for streaming chunks, with no more than 2% error/regression in output quality measured by our fuzzy-match eval.
06:44 Lara Chen: makes sense. recap: mateo runs the benchmarks, we'll share security docs and Dedicated pricing, schedule a POC kickoff. any other blockers?
06:53 Marta Gómez: need to confirm who will own the infra creds; sanjay and i will sort it.
06:57 Sanjay Patel: yep i'll circulate a service-account and a sample model + prompt set.
07:01 Lara Chen: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
07:05 transcript end
